issues.item: Survival Guilt: I feel guilty for surviving when others did not
issues.explanation: For trauma type 'physical abuse by romantic partner', the appraisal 'I feel guilty for surviving when others did not' is clinically hard to reconcile because this trauma does not ordinarily involve other deaths or a mass-casualty context. The rest of the profile centers on partner violence, hypervigilance, and fragmented visual recall, so this item introduces a markedly different trauma scenario without support elsewhere in the selected items.

'Car sounds' is difficult to connect clinically to the rest of this profile for physical abuse by a romantic partner. The other trigger items and all threat, memory, and appraisal items center on interpersonal trauma, bodily alarm, betrayal, and fragmented terror-based recall. A car-sound trigger suggests a different trauma context unless there is supporting material elsewhere, so this item is the main coherence concern.

vignette: Ravi, a 41-year-old South Asian architect, has been experiencing significant distress following physical abuse from his romantic partner. The trauma of that event continues to intrude on his daily life, shaping his thoughts and behaviors in ways that are profoundly affecting both his personal relationships and professional responsibilities. The traumatic incident occurred about six months ago when Ravi returned home late one evening after a long day at the office. As he entered his home, his partner, who had been struggling with alcoholism for some time, was intoxicated and highly agitated. The argument that ensued quickly escalated into physical violence, leaving Ravi shaken and bruised both physically and emotionally. Since then, Ravi has found himself constantly on edge, often reacting before he even realizes what is happening. Simple sounds or movements can set off a jolt of fear, and he finds himself easily startled by unexpected noises or sudden movements around him. He worries that his body reacts to perceived danger without giving him time to think, leaving him feeling vulnerable and exposed. Ravi's sleep has also been deeply affected. Every night, as he tries to fall asleep, the need to stay alert keeps him awake. He is haunted by the fear of another attack, making it nearly impossible for him to fully relax. The constant state of vigilance takes a toll on his energy levels and overall well-being. The memories of that violent encounter are vivid and painful. Whenever Ravi thinks about what happened, he experiences an overwhelming sense of terror, as if reliving the event in real time. These memories often come back as fragmented snapshots - clear visual images that replay in his mind like photographs from a nightmare. Each moment is a stark, unyielding image that evokes intense fear and distress. The trauma has also led Ravi to question his own judgment and abilities. He feels an overwhelming sense of self-doubt, believing he cannot trust himself to make the right decisions. This uncertainty extends to his role as both a husband and an architect. In his personal life, he fears that he has failed in what he sees as his most important duty - keeping his family safe from harm. Professionally, Ravi's work as an architect is increasingly affected by these feelings of self-doubt. He finds it hard to concentrate on complex projects and often double-checks his designs out of fear of making mistakes. The meticulous nature of his job requires a level of confidence that he no longer feels capable of maintaining. Ravi has become highly sensitive to certain triggers that remind him of the abuse - feeling physically unwell, hearing incomprehensible chatter (often mimicking the incoherent arguments from his partner), and even the smell of alcohol. These triggers can set off intense panic attacks or feelings of extreme vulnerability. In his daily life as an architect, he finds himself avoiding social events where alcohol is served, leading to strained relationships with colleagues who do not understand his avoidance. Ravi's marriage has also suffered as a result of this trauma. He feels betrayed by someone he trusted deeply and now struggles to maintain intimacy or trust in their relationship. The constant fear and doubt have created a rift between them that both parties find difficult to bridge. What finally pushed Ravi to seek help was the cumulative toll these symptoms were taking on his life. He realized that if left unchecked, his fears and doubts could potentially derail not just his personal relationships but also his career. Despite his reservations about therapy, he is hopeful that with support, he can regain some sense of control over his life. Ravi's journey towards healing will involve addressing the intense memories and triggers that have dominated his thoughts and actions since the traumatic event. He hopes to find a way to trust himself again and rebuild the relationships in his life that were so deeply affected by this experience.
